reason: The in-guest run needs PowerShell Direct (Invoke-Command / New-PSSession / Copy-Item -ToSession). The agent that prepared this lab ran in a worktree-isolated harness that refused every PowerShell invocation, so nothing was created, started or measured in the lab VM and nothing on the host was changed. Every in-guest check below is BLOCKED, not PASS or FAIL.

guest.os: not collected (the guest was never entered)
guest.approvalScope: administrator actions inside the disposable guest only; unsigned self-contained binaries pinned by SHA-256 (recorded deviation from signed-only); no network, no downloads

hostSideEvidence: Broker pipe DACL (live, same user): owner = Broker SID; Broker allow ACE (PipeAccessRights.FullControl 0x1f019f); for a Control Plane SID that is a different principal, exactly one more allow ACE with mask 0x00120083 (no FILE_APPEND_DATA, no generic right). With the Control Plane SID equal to the Broker's own SID, or malformed, no extra ACE (test/runtime-windows-broker-control-plane-ace.test.mjs, 3/3).

Shim 'inproc' mode hosts the real Broker assembly: the pipe server PID equals the host process PID and the pipe client helper accepts it with owner + PID, one journal claim (test/runtime-windows-service-lab.test.mjs).

Shim 'child' mode launches the Broker as a child: the pipe server PID is the child, not the shim, so the helper expecting the launcher PID (what SCM would report for a launcher service) gets server_identity_mismatch and no claim; expecting the child PID succeeds.
Squatter probe: the helper refuses an owner mismatch before sending and the squatter receives 0 bytes (same-user host test, FOREIGN owner SID expected).
Shim child mode: stdout, exit code and own token captured to a result file; stdin file fed to the helper; a command that does not end is killed on timeout (exit -2).
Not host-testable: StartServiceCtrlDispatcher / RegisterServiceCtrlHandlerEx path (needs the SCM), virtual accounts, restricted service SID, cross-account access.

findings.text: The pipe client helper compares the SCM-reported service PID with GetNamedPipeServerProcessId. A launcher service that starts the Broker as a child reports the launcher's PID, so a correct Broker is refused with server_identity_mismatch. The Broker must be the SCM service process itself. The Broker prototype is a plain exe (no StartServiceCtrlDispatcher); the lab tool hosts its assembly in-process as a stand-in. Host-tested, not service-tested.

With the Broker service not RUNNING the helper's SCM lookup fails first and reports server_identity_unavailable (pre-send), not server_identity_mismatch as lab step 4a first bullet expected. The owner mismatch is observable only while the service is RUNNING and another principal holds the pipe name; the lab script covers both. Derived from reading the helper source (ServicePid runs before CreateFile); not measured in a service.

A client that connects and hangs up without sending a frame makes the Broker write its denial to a closed pipe and end with an unhandled IOException (exit code 0xE0434352 as a child process). Fail-closed (no claim), but not the clean exit the code comments suggest. Observed on the host while writing the DACL test; not changed here.
